recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-19000 unless a new Clinical Genomics issue revisits current MolecularDefinition location or interval semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-19000 was Published/Persuasive for the STU3 Sequence artifact and requested changing referenceSeq.windowStart and referenceSeq.windowEnd from 1..1 to 0..1 when a reference sequence is known but the window is not available.
initial_application: The Jira-cited GH#7f860bf trail is present locally: implementation commit 9c23a7fb0f8197559bfa229b4beab313a017d729 changed source/molecularsequence/molecularsequence-spreadsheet.xml so MolecularSequence.referenceSeq.windowStart and MolecularSequence.referenceSeq.windowEnd moved from 1..1 to 0..1, and merge commit 7f860bf8648888c27d85c440df358f8b2b47a40f brought it in.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini comments out molecularsequence and activates moleculardefinition. Later Published work, especially FHIR-37486 and PR #2030, reframed the old reference-sequence model toward IM-aligned starting-sequence concepts. Current source contains no active referenceSeq/windowStart/windowEnd paths, and MolecularDefinition coordinate interval start/end elements are already optional.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The remaining STU3/R3 history entries showing Sequence.windowStart/windowEnd as 1..1 are preserved historical release artifacts, while R4/R4B MolecularSequence history shows the requested 0..1 cardinalities and current source has no stale mandatory old window elements.

related_jiras.note: Published R5 work renamed/reframed MolecularSequence relative reference elements toward starting-sequence terminology and explains why the old referenceSeq.windowStart/windowEnd paths are not current source.
